title: Definitions and the Hierarchy
summary: Definition as the last step of concept-formation, and concepts as a hierarchy rather than a pile.

lessons.title: The last step
lessons.objective: Place a definition after concept-formation: the units are integrated first, and the definition then states what kind they are.

exercises.prompt: In this account, when does a definition come?

choices.text: After the concept has been formed from its units
Before any units have been noticed
Instead of looking at the units
Whenever a feeling about the word is strong

feedback.note: Forming the concept comes first. The definition is the last step: a statement of the units you have already integrated.

exercises.prompt: What is a definition supposed to do?

choices.text: State the nature of the units the concept refers to
Replace those units with a word
Invent a new kind of existent
Record a vote about how the word should sound

feedback.note: A definition identifies what the units are. It does not create them, and it is not a substitute for them.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to the job it has in this unit.

pairs.right: The existents the concept refers to
The integration of those units
The closing statement of what the units are
A label, not yet a definition

feedback.note: Units, concept, and definition are three steps. A word by itself has not done the last step.

exercises.prompt: Complete the study line.

feedback.note: You do not start with a formula and then hunt for things that fit it. You end with a formula that states the concept.

exercises.prompt: Build the study line.

feedback.note: The line names the job of a definition: to state the nature of the units, not to replace them with a wish.

exercises.prompt: You memorize a formula and never connect it to any units. What do you have?

choices.text: A form of words without the concept it should state
A finished concept
A percept
An axiom of existence

feedback.note: The last step still has to point back to the units. A detached formula is not yet a definition of a concept.

exercises.prompt: Which of these is not what a definition is?

choices.text: A list of every trait the units happen to have
A statement of the nature of the units
The last step after the concept is formed
A way to keep this kind distinct from other kinds

feedback.note: A definition condenses the concept. It does not dump every observed detail into one sentence.

exercises.prompt: Complete the study line.

parts.text: The definition keeps the concept tied to

feedback.note: Without the units, the definition has nothing to state. Its job is to mark the kind those units are.

lessons.title: Genus and differentia
lessons.objective: Build a definition from a genus, the wider group, and a differentia, the characteristic that sets these units apart inside that group.

exercises.prompt: In a definition, the genus is:

choices.text: The wider group from which these units were set apart
The mark that sets these units apart
Any synonym of the word being defined
The mood the word suggests

feedback.note: The genus names the broader concept. The differentia then says how these units differ inside it.

exercises.prompt: The differentia is:

choices.text: The characteristic that distinguishes these units within the genus
Another name for the genus
Every characteristic the units possess
The sound of the word

feedback.note: Genus without a differentia is only the wider group. The differentia is what makes the definition distinguish this concept.

exercises.prompt: Match each piece of the definition of man used in this philosophy.

pairs.right: The full definition
The genus
The differentia
Not the definition used here

feedback.note: Man is stated as a rational animal: animal is the wider group, and rational is the distinguishing characteristic.

exercises.prompt: Complete the study line.

feedback.note: Both parts are required. A wider label alone, or a distinguishing word with no wider group, is not yet this kind of definition.

exercises.prompt: Build the study line for the definition of man.

feedback.note: Rational is the differentia and animal is the genus. Featherless is a surface mark, not the differentia this philosophy uses.

exercises.prompt: Someone says man is an animal, and stops. What is wrong?

choices.text: The genus is there, but the differentia is missing, so the statement is too wide
The statement names too few species to be a genus
Nothing: the genus by itself is a full definition
The statement uses the word man inside itself

feedback.note: Animal includes more than man. Without a differentia, the units of this concept are not distinguished from other animals.

exercises.prompt: Man is a human being. Why does that fail as a definition?

choices.text: It circles back to the same concept instead of stating genus and differentia
Human being names a wider genus than animal
It names a characteristic deeper than rationality
It is a proper differentia

feedback.note: A synonym, or the same idea under another name, does not distinguish the units. It repeats the concept.

exercises.prompt: Match each faulty line to the fault.

pairs.right: Too wide: genus only

pairs.left: Man is a New York banker
pairs.right: Too narrow: drops most of the units
Circular: restates the same concept

feedback.note: Too wide, too narrow, and circular are three ways a line can fail to state genus and differentia for the actual units.

lessons.title: The fundamental characteristic
lessons.objective: Select the fundamental distinguishing characteristic, the one that explains the others, rather than a surface mark.

exercises.prompt: Which characteristic belongs in the differentia?

choices.text: The fundamental one: it explains the greatest number of the other characteristics
The oddest surface mark you can find
Whatever you happened to notice first
All of the characteristics, listed together

feedback.note: Essential here means fundamental. The differentia is the characteristic on which the others of this kind depend.

exercises.prompt: Why does this philosophy take rational, not featherless, as the differentia of man?

choices.text: The rational faculty explains the distinctively human characteristics
Feathers are rarer than reason
Rational is a shorter word
A tradition voted featherless out

feedback.note: Language, science, and production depend on the capacity to reason. Lacking feathers does not explain those characteristics.

exercises.prompt: Match each characteristic of man to the role it plays in a definition.

pairs.right: Fundamental differentia
Genus, the wider group
Not the explaining characteristic
A surface mark, not the differentia

feedback.note: A true mark can still be the wrong differentia. The one that belongs in the definition is the one that explains the rest.

exercises.prompt: Complete the study line.

parts.text: The fundamental characteristic is the one that

feedback.note: If a trait does not explain the others, it can distinguish by accident and still not be the essential differentia.

exercises.prompt: Build the study line.

feedback.note: Genus and differentia are not enough if the differentia is a decoration. It has to be the fundamental distinguishing characteristic.

exercises.prompt: A student defines man by listing rationality, thumbs, earlobes, and city of birth. What is the mistake?

choices.text: A definition states the fundamental differentia, not a pile of traits
The list is too short to be a genus
None of those traits can be true of the units
City of birth is the genus

feedback.note: Extra true details do not improve the definition. They bury the characteristic that explains the kind.

exercises.prompt: Two groups of animals differ in color, and that color explains none of their other differences. Color is:

choices.text: A surface mark, not the fundamental differentia
Fundamental, because you can see it at once
The genus of both groups
The concept itself, so no definition is needed

feedback.note: Visibility is not fundamentality. The differentia has to carry the other characteristics, not merely be easy to point at.

exercises.prompt: Complete the study line.

feedback.note: That dependence is what fundamental means in a definition. The rest of the kind is understood through that characteristic.

lessons.title: A hierarchy, not a pile
lessons.objective: Treat concepts as a hierarchy in which later concepts rest on earlier ones, not as a flat pile of labels.

exercises.prompt: How are concepts ordered in this unit?

choices.text: In a hierarchy: later concepts rest on earlier ones
In a pile: every label is on the same level
Only by alphabetical order of the words
By how strongly you like the word

feedback.note: A pile would make every concept available at once. A hierarchy means some concepts are the base on which others are formed.

exercises.prompt: You form the concept furniture from concepts such as table, chair, and bed. Which way does the dependence run?

choices.text: Furniture rests on those earlier concepts, not the other way around
Table is valid only after furniture has been defined
The four words are one concept
None of them depends on observation

feedback.note: Wider concepts are integrations of earlier ones. Table can be formed from perceived tables before furniture is formed.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to its place in the hierarchy.

pairs.right: The base from which the concept table is formed
Earlier than the wider concept furniture
A later integration of concepts such as table and chair
Not the order of concepts

feedback.note: The hierarchy runs from observed units up through earlier concepts to wider ones. A word list erases that order.

exercises.prompt: Complete the study line.

feedback.note: If a concept had no earlier base, it would be a loose label. In this account, later concepts rest on earlier ones.

exercises.prompt: Build the study line.

feedback.note: Hierarchy is the order. A pile would treat every concept as independent of the ones it was formed from.

exercises.prompt: Someone defines table as a kind of furniture, while furniture is itself understood only as tables, chairs, and beds. What went wrong?

choices.text: A later concept was used as if it were the base of an earlier one
Furniture cannot ever be a genus
Nothing: every concept may define the concepts it rests on
The differentia should have been a color

feedback.note: A definition has to be stated with concepts that are earlier in the hierarchy. Using a later concept as the base turns the order upside down.

exercises.prompt: Which learning order matches the hierarchy?

choices.text: Observed tables, then the concept table, then the wider concept furniture
The word furniture first, with no earlier concepts
A dictionary list, memorized from A to Z
Whichever word feels most abstract today

feedback.note: Earlier concepts are available before the wider ones that integrate them. The hierarchy is an order of dependence, not an alphabetical list.

exercises.prompt: Match each rule to the hierarchy.

pairs.right: Must be earlier than the concept defined

pairs.left: A concept formed from this one
pairs.right: Cannot be the base that defines it
Erases which concepts can define which

feedback.note: Definition uses the hierarchy. The terms in the definition have to stand under the concept, not above it.

lessons.title: Context and the same units
lessons.objective: See that a definition states the fundamentals in the order of one's knowledge, and can be restated when that knowledge deepens without dropping the units.

exercises.prompt: A definition states essentials in relation to what?

choices.text: The context of one's knowledge, in hierarchical order
A wording that can never be improved
Each person's private stipulation
Whatever most speakers prefer this year

feedback.note: You can state only the fundamentals your knowledge has reached, and only with concepts earlier than the one you are defining.

exercises.prompt: Knowledge grows, and a deeper fundamental of the same units is discovered. What may change?

choices.text: The wording of the definition, so that it states the deeper fundamental
The units, which must be replaced by a new kind
Nothing: the first wording is final even if it missed the fundamental
The rule that a definition needs a genus

feedback.note: A better context can yield a better statement of the same concept. The definition is revised because knowledge of the units deepened, not because the units were voted away.

exercises.prompt: After a valid definition is restated for a deeper fundamental, the concept still refers to:

choices.text: The same kind of units
No units at all
Only the new word, with the old referents dropped
The speaker's new feeling about the word

feedback.note: Changing the statement is not changing the subject. The concept remains the integration of those units.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to what a deeper context does with it.

pairs.right: May be restated to name the deeper fundamental
Stay the referents if they are still that kind
Still requires earlier concepts in the definition
Still not the order of concepts

feedback.note: Context lets the definition improve. It does not flatten the hierarchy or cut the concept off from its units.

exercises.prompt: Complete the study line.

parts.text: When knowledge deepens, the definition can be

feedback.note: Restating is not starting over. The new statement still has to cover the units the concept was formed from.

exercises.prompt: Build the study line.

feedback.note: Contextual means it states what is fundamental in the knowledge one has. Hierarchical means the terms it uses are earlier concepts.

exercises.prompt: Which revision is allowed?

choices.text: Naming a deeper fundamental of the same units, with earlier concepts
Rewriting the definition to match a wish about the units
Defining the concept by a concept that rests on it
Keeping the wording and dropping the referents

feedback.note: Growth of knowledge is not a license to stipulate. The new definition still has to be fundamental, hierarchical, and about those units.

exercises.prompt: What does this unit hold together?

choices.text: Definition as the last step, and concepts as a hierarchy rather than a pile
The senses as the only direct contact with reality
The three axiomatic concepts as the start of metaphysics
Emotions as tools that replace definitions

feedback.note: The last step states the concept. The hierarchy decides which concepts that statement may use, and keeps every concept on a base rather than in a pile.
